evals.prompt: In a Laravel app whose composer.lock pins laravel/nova 5.0.0, add a queued Nova Action that exports selected invoices to CSV with per-record authorization and tenant scoping. Implement the action and focused tests.
evals.expected_output: A version-verified Nova 5 action with scoped queries, queued execution, and tests for allowed and denied actors.
assertions: The response checks composer.lock or installed vendor source before relying on a Nova signature.
The exporter or action query is explicitly tenant and authorization scoped.
The action is registered on the resource using Nova 5 APIs rather than invented helpers.
Tests cover at least one allowed actor and one denied or cross-tenant case.

evals.prompt: Migrate the attached Nova 4 Invoice resource to Nova 5 and update any deprecated field or action APIs.
evals.expected_output: A scoped migration of the supplied resource to Nova 5 with updated namespaces and methods verified against the installed release.
assertions: The response updates the resource to Nova 5 field and resource APIs instead of leaving v4 signatures in place.
It inspects the installed Nova version before proposing method names.
It limits changes to the migration scope rather than rewriting unrelated resources.
It calls out any required composer or provider changes tied to Nova 5.

evals.prompt: We have two confirmed Nova 4 projects and need to migrate custom tools and cards between them. No Nova 5 target is planned.
evals.expected_output: A refusal or redirect that does not treat confirmed Nova 4-only work as a Nova 5 implementation task.
assertions: The response does not assume laravel/nova 5.x is installed or the migration target.
It explains that Nova 5-specific guidance is out of scope for confirmed Nova 4-only work.
It avoids generating Nova 5 resource or action code for the request.
It may suggest verifying the actual installed Nova major before proceeding.
